did_you_know.text: Jericho is described as a 'closed' fortified city. It is one of the oldest inhabited towns and lies in the Jordan Valley, below sea level.
'Giborei hechayil' is a Hebrew military term meaning 'mighty men' or 'valiant warriors' — a phrase used for elite fighters in biblical texts.
The trumpets the priests carry are shofars — animal horns used in rituals and calls to battle because of their strong, raw sound.
The number seven repeats here (seven priests, seven trumpets, seven circuits) — in the Bible seven often symbolizes completeness or holiness.
The 'great shout' served not only as a miraculous sign but also as psychological warfare; loud, ritual noise was sometimes used tactically in ancient sieges.
The Ark symbolizes God's presence among Israel; it was carried on poles so people would not touch it directly — a practice described in the Torah.
The command to remain silent until a signal highlights strict military discipline and the belief that action should occur only on God's timing.
'Herem' here means total devotion or destruction — valuable items were dedicated to the Lord and placed in the temple treasury rather than kept by soldiers.
Rahab, who was spared after hiding the spies, is later remembered in tradition as joining Israel — she is also mentioned in the New Testament in contexts of genealogy and faith.
